description: Answer key for check_citations.py and the tests/model_right_sizer/test_citation_fidelity.py suite. One entry per research paper the model-right-sizer agent (agents/model-right-sizer.md) cites for a formula or a numeric claim. Five independent bindings, each mechanically checked: (1) `citation_substring`/`exact_substring` -- literal, character-for-character presence in the agent file, binding the AGENT PROSE to this ledger; (2) `numbers`-bearing claims are recomputed and compared against the claimed value; (3) `formula_expr` evaluated on each sample's `inputs` vs. actually calling `module.primary_function(**inputs)`, binding this ledger to the SHIPPED IMPLEMENTATION; (4) `source_variables` -- the declared free-variable set a claim's equation should reference, diffed against formula_expr's actual free variables (via ast), binding formula_expr to what the human-authored `source_quote` independently says the equation contains; (5) each sample's `expected_output` -- computed by hand from the paper's stated formula, independently of both `formula_expr` and the implementation (see the git history of this file for the one-off derivation script) -- checked against BOTH of them. (5) is what (3)+(4) alone can't provide: (3) only proves formula_expr and the implementation agree with EACH OTHER, and (4) only proves formula_expr's variable SET matches what's declared -- neither catches formula_expr and the implementation being edited TOGETHER to the same wrong structure (a sign flip, a swapped term, a transposed pairing) that still uses the correct variable names. expected_output is authored once, from the confirmed-correct source_quote, and stored in a THIRD place neither of the other two edits touches, so a coordinated drift now has to also falsify an independently-computed number to pass. What this file still does NOT mechanically verify: that `source_quote` itself is a faithful transcription of the live arXiv PDF -- that was checked by hand against the fetched paper at authoring time (each claim cites its exact section/equation/figure) and is a residual human/primary-source trust boundary, the same class of gap `verifiable: false` already names elsewhere in this file; no finite set of cross-checks fully closes that without re-deriving the paper's own math from scratch. Update this file in the same PR as any edit to the agent file's cited numbers/formulas or to token_economics.py / reasoning_budget.py, and let the tests catch drift between all of them.

papers.title: Think Smarter, not Harder: Adaptive Reasoning with Inference-Aware Optimization
papers.cited_for: difficulty-adaptive effort -- do not reason uniformly

claims.exact_substring: +4.14–5.74% absolute MATH500 accuracy at a fixed 2–4× budget
claims.note: The gain/budget figures are reported as a range, not a single formula input -- the test asserts the low/high pairs are each positive and correctly ordered (low <= high), and that eval/reasoning_budget.accuracy_per_compute(gain, budget) is internally consistent at both ends of the range (4.14/2 = 2.07, 5.74/4 = 1.435).

claims.verification_note: Verifying this ratio exactly requires the paper's self-consistency baseline's own accuracy-per-compute figure (a results-table number), which was not present in the excerpt this ledger was built from. eval/reasoning_budget.ibpo_accuracy_per_compute_gain() computes the ratio honestly given both inputs; it is never invoked with a fabricated baseline. Keep `verifiable: false` until the baseline figure is sourced from the paper's actual results table -- do not flip this to true on the strength of the citation alone.

papers.title: Empowering Budget-aware LLM Reasoning with Control Tokens
papers.cited_for: explicit budget + graded adherence -- signal the budget, don't just hope

claims.exact_substring: length-aware reward that optimizes accuracy AND budget adherence at once
claims.verification_note: The paper describes the reward's objective in prose, not a closed-form weight split -- budget_control_token_reward() is model-right-sizer's own literal operationalization of that description (a weighted sum, the simplest function meeting it), not a formula transcribed from the paper's own equations. formula_expr/source_variables/expected_output here check that the *function* matches model-right-sizer's own stated operationalization (drift protection on our own code), not that the operationalization matches the paper (which is why `verifiable` stays false against the source).

papers.title: Token Economics for LLM Agents: A Dual-View Study from Computing and Economics
papers.authors: Chen, Chen, He, Li, Ji, Wu, Yang, Diao, Shou, Zhang, Li, Chen
papers.cited_for: the economic formalism the effectiveness-vs-efficiency split is an instance of

claims.source_quote: TC = P_k · K + P_m · M + w · L

the elasticity of substitution is defined as σ = 1/(1−ρ). As ρ → 1 (where σ → ∞), the factors become perfect substitutes ... as ρ → −∞ (where σ → 0), the factors exhibit rigid complementarity. This extreme boundary characterizes the "Memory Wall"
the shadow price is defined as P̃_int/ext = P_m + w · τ_inf, where P_m denotes the per-token procurement price, and τ_inf accounts for inference latency or tool-invocation overhead
extended in Section 4 to P̃_comm = P_m + w · τ_sync + ΔC_coord, which incorporates inter-agent synchronization latency (τ_sync) and the coordination costs associated with format alignment (ΔC_coord)

in Section 5, the model converges to P̃_eco = P_m + w · τ_cong + C_comp, further encompassing congestion latency (τ_cong) induced by multi-tenant competition, as well as costs related to system compliance and environmental externalities (C_comp)
Optimal Point E*, MRTS = P̃_ext/P̃_int; Slope = -P̃_ext/P̃_int
GraphRAG provides a canonical capital-leverage calculation: fixed indexing investment I_graph is justified when I_graph / Q < ΔY per query

claims.exact_substring: 0.4 trillion in December 2024 to 27.0 trillion by March 2026, a nearly 68-fold increase in 15 months
claims.note: This is the source paper's own headline stat, not one model-right-sizer.md repeats in its prose. Kept in the ledger as a standing example of holding a source document's own arithmetic to the same code-checked standard: 27.0/0.4 = 67.5, which is what 'nearly 68-fold' should mean -- the test asserts the computed multiple falls within a small tolerance of the claimed 68.
